overview: Luxembourg is a small landlocked country between Belgium, France and Germany. Its capital, Luxembourg City, is one of the official seats of the European Union. It is the only grand duchy left in the world, and its official languages are Luxembourgish, French and German. Luxembourg has one of the highest incomes per person in the world, thanks largely to banking and finance.

geography.text: The north of Luxembourg, called the Ösling, is part of the forested Ardennes uplands. The south, called the Gutland or 'good land', is lower and more fertile, and is where most people live. The Moselle river forms part of the border with Germany, and its valley is lined with vineyards.

history.text: Luxembourg began as a castle built in 963. Over the centuries it was ruled by Burgundy, Spain, Austria and France. It became a grand duchy in 1815 and was declared permanently neutral in 1867. Occupied by Germany in both World Wars, it then became a founding member of NATO and of what is now the European Union.

events.title: Castle founded
events.text: Count Siegfried acquires the rock on which Luxembourg City grows.

events.title: Grand duchy
events.text: The Congress of Vienna makes Luxembourg a grand duchy.

events.title: Neutrality
events.text: The Treaty of London declares Luxembourg permanently neutral.

events.title: German occupation
events.text: Germany occupies Luxembourg during the Second World War.

events.title: Founding member of the EEC
events.text: Luxembourg helps found what becomes the European Union.
